subject: Calling values into the lavaan model

messages.author: a59d7be71cc9924a
messages.subject: Calling values into the lavaan model
parts:
I'm trying to set certain factor loadings.  I'm not 100% on what those values will be yet, and they are calculated outside of lavaan.

Is there a way to set up a generic lavaan model that will import a value from outside lavaan?

So something like:

dat$x <- .5 #to be set/updated by a preceding function
dat$y <- .6 #to be set/updated by a preceding function

model <- ‘y1 ~ (dat$x)*x1 + (dat$y)x2’

Thanks,
Dave

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Calling values into the lavaan model
parts: Is there a way to set up a generic lavaan model that will import a value from outside lavaan?

Not like that.  Previous posts on this forum have talked about 2 methods:
  • using the paste() function to specify the skeleton of your model syntax, with variables for the values you want to paste into the syntax
  • creating a parameter table from the syntax, then updating the value(s) in the parameter table (which is a data.frame; see ?parTable and ?lavaanify).
I think another easy solution would be to label the parameters in your model syntax, then you can use the constraints argument to specify what those labels should equal.

model <- ' y1 ~ a*x1 + b*x2 '
fit <- lavaan(model, data, constraints = c('a == .5','b == .6'), ...)

Of course, you can still use paste() to make the constraints. 

myParams <- 
myConstraints <- paste(c('a','b'), "==", myParams)
fit <- lavaan(model, data, constraints = myConstraints, ...)

parts:
Dave,

Here is the parameter table method mentioned by Terrence.

require(lavaan)

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

HS.param <- lavaanify(HS.model) # Obtain parameter table

fixedLoading <- read.table(<myFile>)  # Read fixed loading values from file (this line is pseudocode)

HS.param$ustart[1] <- fixedLoading[1] # Insert desired values into parameter table.  This is just an example.

fit <- cfa(HS.param, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)  # Fit parameter table directly.
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)

Keith
